title: Mercedes' clever new driving assist handles complex traffic like a champ
gist: Mercedes-Benz is rolling out MB. Drive Assist Pro, a 'level 2++' point-to-point assisted driving system for complex urban traffic, built on MB.OS and Nvidia's Orin hardware and Alpamayo end-to-end driving stack, with early access in Germany and California next month and wider rollout in H1 2027. The reviewer found it Waymo-smooth and appropriately cautious.

insights.claim: L2+ systems combining driver monitoring with hands-free operation on geofenced highways have been the main driver-assist development, led by GM's Super Cruise and followed by Ford BlueCruise and BMW Highway Assistant.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Hands-free highway assist is becoming table stakes; differentiation moves to urban capability.

insights.claim: Mercedes will add hands-free highway assist to MB. Drive Assist next spring, standard on the 2027 S-Class and AMG GT 4-Door Coupe and optional on the 2027 CLA, GLB, C-Class, GLC and GLE.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Broad trim availability expands Mercedes' software-feature revenue base.
insights.locator: General Motors’ Super Cruise was the first

insights.claim: Mercedes' Drive Assist Pro, a 'level 2++' point-to-point system, handled San Francisco surface streets as smoothly as a Waymo robotaxi, safely passing double-parked cars and stopping for signs, lights and pedestrians.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Supervised urban assist from an OEM narrows the experiential gap with robotaxis.
insights.locator: The driving behavior was about exactly as cautious

insights.claim: Drive Assist Pro is collaborative—steering or accelerating doesn't end automation—but any brake use turns it off, unlike BMW's new iX5.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Design choices on handover differentiate OEM systems and affect safety perception.

insights.claim: Drive Assist Pro enters early access for some customers in Germany and California next month, with wider rollout in the first half of 2027 across CLA, GLC Electric, GLE, GLS and S-Class, and is already live in China.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Rollout timing marks when Mercedes' software-defined features hit US revenue.
insights.locator: Some customers in Germany and California

insights.claim: Drive Assist Pro uses 10 cameras, five radars and 12 ultrasonic sensors fused by a domain controller on Nvidia Orin processors delivering 254 TOPS, with a 2.5 Gbit Ethernet network and over 70GB of RAM.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Confirms Nvidia's automotive compute design wins at a premium OEM.

insights.claim: Driving decisions in Mercedes' system come from Nvidia's Alpamayo end-to-end tokenized stack, with a rules-based system running alongside as a safety check, and the Nvidia stack is certified by Germany's TÜV.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Nvidia is moving beyond chips into the driving software layer for OEMs, expanding its automotive TAM.
insights.quote: Nvidia’s Alpamayo end-to-end tokenized stack that picks your driving trajectory, with a rules-based system running alongside as a safety check

insights.claim: Mercedes' MB.OS reflects the software-defined vehicle shift of replacing dozens or hundreds of ECUs with a few powerful domain controllers for dynamics, comfort, infotainment and automation.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Centralized compute architectures shift auto value toward high-end processors and software.
insights.locator: The unifying factor is the MB.OS

insights.claim: In China, cars are now reportedly advertised by processor and RAM specs rather than range or performance.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Compute specs as a selling point favors chip suppliers in the Chinese auto market.
